message.content:
**The Kiss** by Auguste Rodin (1889) is widely regarded as the most iconic and celebrated sculpture of the 19th century. ### Why it stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading French sculptor who bridged Romanticism and modernism | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist – a highly expressive, almost photographic rendering of a couple in an intimate embrace | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and sensuality worldwide.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums, galleries, and public spaces.
• Its dramatic pose and emotional depth made it instantly recognizable and commercially successful. | | **Legacy** | • The sculpture has been reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media.
• It remains a benchmark for evaluating 19th‑century sculpture and is frequently cited in art history texts. | ### Other contenders - **The Gates of Hell** (unfinished, 1880–1908) – a monumental bronze group that showcases Rodin’s mastery of complex human forms. - **Statue of Liberty** (1886) – a monumental public monument by Frédéric Bartholdi, symbolizing freedom and democracy. - **The Thinker** (1902) – technically a 20th‑century work, but often grouped with Rodin’s 19th‑century output. While several masterpieces share the spotlight, **The Kiss** remains the most universally recognized and celebrated sculpture from the 19th century.
